prerequisites: Computer Science: Computer Science for Engineering (V12G380V01203)
Mathematics: Calculus II and Differential Equations (V12G380V01204)
To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses lower than the one in which this course is placed.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire a global and realistic vision of the current scope of industrial automation systems.
Understand the constituent elements of an industrial automation system, how they work, and how they are sized.
Applied knowledge of programmable logic controllers, their programming, and their application to industrial system automation.
General knowledge of continuous control of dynamic systems, the main simulation tools for continuous systems, and the main process control devices of greatest industrial interest.
General concepts of industrial controller tuning techniques.

syllabus_topics: 1. Introduction to industrial automation and automation elements.
1.4 Block diagram. Elements of the programmable controller.
2. Languages and programming techniques for programmable logic controllers.
2.1 Binary, octal, hexadecimal, BCD system. Real numbers.
2.7 Binary variables. Inputs, outputs and memory.
3.2.1 Definition of stages and transitions. Evolution rules.
4.2 Typical control loop. Nomenclature and definitions.
5. Representation, modeling and simulation of continuous dynamic systems.
5.3 Transfer function modeling. Laplace transform. Properties. Examples.
6.2.1 First-order systems. Differential equation and transfer function. Examples.
6.2.2 Second-order systems. Differential equation and transfer function. Examples.
6.2.3 Effect of adding poles and zeros.
7. PID controller. Tuning of industrial controller parameters.
7.1 Basic control actions. Proportional, integral, and derivative effects.
7.3 Empirical methods for tuning industrial controllers.
7.3.1 Open-loop tuning formulas: Ziegler-Nichols and others.
7.3.2 Closed-loop tuning formulas: Ziegler-Nichols and others.
7.4 Design of state-variable controllers. Pole assignment.
P1. Introduction to TIA Portal and STEP 7. Introduction to the TIA Portal program, which allows creating and modifying programs for Siemens S7-1200 and S7-1500 controllers.
P2. Programming in TIA Portal. Modeling of a simple automation example and implementation in STEP7 using binary operations.
P3. Implementation of RdP in TIA Portal. Modeling with RdP of a simple automation example and introduction to its implementation in TIA Portal.
P4. Modeling with RdP and implementation in TIA Portal. Modeling with RdP of a medium complexity automation example and its implementation in TIA Portal.
P5. Modeling with GRAFCET and implementation with Graph. Standardized modeling of an RdP and implementation of automation systems with Graph.
P6. Analysis of control systems with MATLAB. Introduction to specific control system instructions of the MATLAB program.
P7. Introduction to SIMULINK. Introduction to the SIMULINK program, a MATLAB extension for dynamic system simulation.
P8. Modeling and temporal response in SIMULINK. Modeling and simulation of control systems with SIMULINK.
P9. Empirical tuning of an industrial controller. Determination of PID controller parameters by the studied methods and implementation of the calculated control in an industrial controller.
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation of laboratory work is mandatory. If not passed, a practical exam will be held in the second call, conditioned on passing the written test. For students who officially waive continuous evaluation, a practical exam will be held in both calls, conditioned on passing the written test. Both the written exam (80%) and the laboratory practices (20%) must be passed to approve the course; if either is not passed, the total grade may be scaled down to a maximum of 4.5. In the final exam, a minimum score may be required for certain questions. In the second call, students must take the written and/or practical exams not passed in the first call, using the same criteria. Unethical behavior will result in a failing grade (0.0) for the entire academic year.
